startup.name: Sherpa Labs
startup.description: No description beyond the one liner Frontier Data. Tags: reinforcement learning, data labeling, AI. Five person team in San Francisco, B2B, assumed to sell training data, RL environments and expert labeling to frontier AI labs.

yc_acceptance.basis: Prior of about 1 percent (yc_acceptance.md, range 0.6 to 2 percent). Up for an AI data niche fitting YC's AI focus and a five person team; down because the pitch is a single phrase and data labeling has a dominant incumbent in Scale AI. Net about 1.5 percent. The company is already in the Winter 2025 batch, shown for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because 'Frontier Data' does not say what is sold, to whom or why a lab would buy from a five person startup instead of Scale AI or Surge, and customer concentration among a few labs is a known risk.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --tag AI --calibration-only: seed 51% / 64% / 71% (cond 64%, n=183); B2B 2022-2025 cond 59% (n=126). time_to_milestones.csv era:2022+ months_to_seed p25 3, median 6, p75 14.2.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 22.4 months from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, long enough for about 85 percent of eventual seeds to land in the 2022+ timing table (p75 is 14 months). The target is an outside round above about $1M, not the YC deal. 0.64 x 0.85 x about 0.95 for the exclusion is 0.52. No lift for sector heat or team size per the winners test; these odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M, common for data companies with a few lab pilots; Lightly raised $3M and Playment $1.6M.
Institutional seed, near Sieve's $4M seed and the 2022+ B2B median of $3.5M.
Larger seed if lab contracts show revenue; confirmed 2026 raises above $1M had median $6.0M but lean high.
Upside if lab demand and a recognized founding team create a hot round.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed fails if demand from labs is lumpy and the company lacks a repeatable edge. Scale AI raised $1B at $13.8B in May 2024 and has deep lab relationships. Past YC data companies split: Centaur reached a $15M Series A and Sieve a $4M seed, while Sepal AI stayed at the $500K YC deal and was acquired. A five person team with no stated product detail may be treated as services, which investors discount.

bands.rationale: Smaller A for a data services business with concentrated customers.
Typical 2022+ A, median $15M, for real revenue from several labs.
Upside A if revenue grows fast on RL environment demand.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A depends on revenue growing beyond one or two lab customers. Data vendors face customer concentration, pricing pressure and labs building in house, and investors discount service-like gross margins. Playment shows a labeling company can raise modest seeds yet not reach the scale of Scale AI.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Reduced from the anchor because the window is short for a Series B; within 2x.

bands.rationale: Modest Series B with strong revenue but high customer concentration among a few labs.
Typical 2022+ Series B round, median $40M, with several labs under contract.
Upside if the company becomes a leading source of RL data.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B is reached by a small share of seed companies, and it requires diversified customers and a data moat, not just labor. If frontier labs vertically integrate or consolidate vendors around Scale AI, Surge and a few others, growth would stall and investors would pass because lab budgets can shift quickly with each model generation.

bands.rationale: Typical Series C round, with the 2022+ table median at $74M and post money near $1.2B.
Strong growth case with scaled revenue and a high valuation near the top of the range.
Flat or down round if lab spending cools.

ladder.why_it_fails: Few data vendors reach this stage. Late stage requires durable demand from labs that may build data in house or buy from fewer vendors; revenue tied to a small number of AI budgets can reverse quickly when a lab changes its training recipe, and a late stage investor would price in that volatility and the risk that Scale AI or an in-house team wins the next contract.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The data vendor market is concentrated around a dominant incumbent and depends on a few lab customers. Small vendors often end in acquisition by a larger data or AI company at modest prices, as Sepal AI did, and a miss on lab demand ends in a stall.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building quality data and RL environments needs domain expertise and pipelines for verifying outputs; a five person team can run a first lab pilot in about 3 months but scaling quality labor is hard.

takeover_risk.rationale: Larger vendors can add similar services quickly, and labs can build in house, but specialized expert data is hard to replicate at speed.

evidence.claim: Scale AI's valuation doubled to $13.8B on a $1B raise in May 2024, showing large paid demand for AI training data.
Capital flowing into foundation model companies drove Scale's revenue growth including RLHF work.

actions: Run a paid pilot with a model team
Document data quality against a benchmark
Sign three paying labs or model builders

pros.point: Large paid market near the frontier
pros.evidence: Scale AI's 2024 round shows investors and labs spend heavily on training data.

brand.rationale: Name plus descriptor forms like Sherpa Labs are common among YC AI companies and neutral for outcomes; the guide metaphor is decent but not distinctive, and buyers are labs who care about quality not names.

narrative.headline: A hot AI data niche with a dominant incumbent and little visible product detail.
narrative.general_summary: Sherpa Labs appears to sell frontier training data to AI labs. The forecast window is 22.4 months from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, long enough for most seed timing. We give 0.52 for an outside round above about $1M closing in the window, from the AI cohort anchor of 0.64 with no hype lift. Analogs split between Centaur and Sieve, which raised, and Sepal AI, which stayed at the YC deal. These odds do not rank this company against others. Reaching a round years later is common for companies with paying customers.
